construct.name: Stèle de souvenir de Lumina Prime v0 (un lieu qui retient ce qui lui est arrivé)
construct.purpose: Hold the LORE of a place — what happened there, and why the place is the way it is — as a sealed, dated, provenance-tagged inscription that reveals itself to a citizen who comes close, and to no one else. A city that cannot remember why its shapes are the shapes they are re-derives the same accident forever. The stele is the smallest civic object that stops that: one stance, one sealed inscription, one reader, one receipt.

inscription_port.honesty: No actor in this store holds authority:inscribe-lore, and no SealedCapabilityPort adjudicates this port yet. The port is DECLARED, not enforced: today the only way a second inscription lands is another bootstrap injection from a terminal. That is an honest gap, not a hidden fallback.
inscription_port.rule: A second memory is added to this stele only by an actor whose GRAPH-HELD capability set (read from its USED edges, never from a self-declared request field) contains authority:inscribe-lore. Reading the stele grants none of it. Adding an inscription re-opens the seal until the new set is re-sealed, so the reveal gate cannot fire on a half-inscribed stele.

root_content.native_law_boundary: AtomDynamics knows only AtomSpec, AtomBond and support/inhibit/neutral. This construct adds no law. The inscription text, its per-claim epistemic status, the reading radius, the cooldown, the seal and the reader's identity are typed payload DATA on things; none is a term in native dispatch. Energy only gates whether a reveal is admitted; it never encodes what the stele remembers, who read it, or how sure the memory is.

parent_scope.justification: A placed civic object awaiting installation under a public-memory registry Space. Exactly one scope classification. NO PART_OF edge is written to a parent, because no containing Space for it exists in this store — and writing one to an unbuilt parent is precisely the kind of un-founded containment this stele's own inscription is about. The stele is an object set down, and it says so.

reveal_contract.effect: exactly one typed `revealed_inscription` stimulus to the exact reader that crossed, carrying the inscription VERBATIM with every claim's epistemic status attached
reveal_contract.never: no loop, no scan, no poll, no timer. A dormant stele costs nothing and is the ordinary state of a stele.
reveal_contract.rule: An unsealed inscription is non-revealable. A stele with a broken seal reveals NOTHING and reports `measurement_failed` — it never reveals a text it cannot prove is the text that was sealed.
reveal_contract.trigger: a citizen body crossing the stele's reading collider — a physical condition placed in the field, reported by the solver for free

stance.honesty: The stele authors NO Built pose. Its place in the city is therefore not a fact of this store: a renderer will show it wherever the layout solver puts it, and that coordinate is `inferred_from_physics`, never `built`. Declaring the stance and leaving it EMPTY is the honest form; writing a coordinate the operator did not choose would make the stele commit, in its own body, the very confusion its first inscription records.

place_reference.why: The lore this stele carries is about a place named only relative to Balise Zéro ('près de la balise d'orientation'). The stele cannot answer 'which place is this about?' without that node. This is an OPERATIONAL dependency (DEPENDS_ON), never containment (PART_OF): a beacon is a point, not a room, and nothing in this store contains either of them.

rearm_semantics.energy_consumption_on_fire: the approach atom's accrued support is consumed to zero on fire, so a single crossing cannot cascade
rearm_semantics.hysteresis: exit is measured at 1.25x the entry radius, so a body standing on the boundary does not oscillate the sensor
rearm_semantics.latch: the reveal gate latches on fire and cannot re-fire until reset
rearm_semantics.reset_condition: the reading collider reports the SAME body has exited the radius
rearm_semantics.why_required: This construct declares environmental feedback (a reveal changes the world, which may produce new physics events). Per the construct protocol, environmental feedback without these seven is self-excitation, and a stele that shouted at everyone standing near it forever would be the loudest object in the city.

steps: stay dormant; hold the reading collider in the field and consume nothing
on a solver-reported crossing, admit the event through the membrane and resolve the crossing body's identity; an unresolved identity is `unknown`, never a default reader
deposit measured energy onto the approach atom via a Support bond stamped energy_status=measured
fire the approach threshold at support >= N
measure the seal over the exact stored inscription bytes; a mismatch ends the run as measurement_failed and reveals NOTHING
measure inscription non-emptiness and dedup-token freshness
run the reveal-gate circuit to quiescence; the gate fires only with all five supports measured
assemble the payload by COPYING the stored claims — statement, epistemic_status, source, measured_by, observed_at_revision, universe — with no transformation of any kind
fire the terminal emitter exactly once and deliver to the exact reader
persist reveal_receipt (payload hash, reader, seal id, emitted_at) and a reading_ledger entry
apply the rearm_semantics: consume the trigger energy, latch, and hold the cooldown before the collider can re-arm for the same body
run the independent observer over the stored inscription, the atom event ledger, the delivered payload and the receipts
PRODUCE the metric vector, each dimension against its spec; an unmeasured dimension is not_measured, never 0
derive health from the FRESH vector, and EVIDENCE the objective_satisfaction claim from that health and nothing else

forbidden: revealing an inscription whose seal is not measured valid
delivering a claim without its epistemic_status
delivering one side of a contested claim
paraphrasing, summarising or re-rendering the inscription on the way out
revealing to anyone but the exact body that crossed
two reveals for one crossing, or a re-fire inside the cooldown
waking on a timer, a scan or a poll
treating the physics crossing as an authorised semantic mutation
claiming delivery from a renderer animation or from an emitter that merely fired
pre-creating validation_run, health_assessment or the satisfaction claim
converting an absent, stale or unreadable inscription into an empty-but-successful reveal
presenting the stele's memory as the world's current state
content.given: A stele carrying at least one inscription whose seal is measured valid, a reading collider placed in the field, an identified citizen body, a fresh dedup token, and measured atom energy on every support.
then: the crossing is lifted to a PhysicsEvent, which mutates nothing
a DepositBond puts MEASURED energy on the approach atom; the atom fires at support >= N
the reveal gate fires only with all five supports measured: approach admitted, reader identified, seal valid, inscription non-empty, dedup token fresh
the terminal emitter surfaces exactly ONE revealed_inscription for that exact reader
the payload carries every claim VERBATIM with its own epistemic_status, source, observed_at_revision and universe
a contested claim is carried WITH its contest and both provenances
a reveal_receipt and a reading_ledger entry are persisted
the gate re-arms only per the declared rearm_semantics; it does not re-fire while the same body loiters on the boundary
an independent observer re-reads the delivered payload against the stored inscription and PRODUCES the metric vector
content.when: A citizen body crosses the reading collider. Never on a timer, never on a scan, never on a query.

reveal_atom_circuit.conservation_note: The emitter is TERMINAL: it conducts only to the receipt and the ledger, and nothing conducts back into the gate. A broken seal streams no energy at all, so an unsealed stele is not merely refused — it is non-conductive, exactly as unsealed ink is in the energetic pen.

content.honesty: This field set is the implementation's own account of itself and is self_reported — never evidence. As authored: the construct is a portable projection, structurally checked locally. graph_status flips to `written` only once an injector commits it and an independent reader confirms it; `wired`, `running`, `verified` and `sealed` are all false and are expected to stay false until the reading collider is actually placed in the physics field, a body actually crosses it, and a signature is actually computed over the inscription bytes. Nothing here should be read as a stele that works.
incoming: maintenance -> repair feedback -> implementation (through the effect protocol)
known_gaps: no reading collider is placed in any physics field: the Sensor is DECLARED, not installed
no signature exists over the inscription, so the seal is `unsealed` and by this construct's own rule the stele would reveal nothing
the inscription port names authority:inscribe-lore, which no actor in this store holds and no SealedCapabilityPort adjudicates
no Built pose: the stele's place in the city is unknown and will be solver-inferred
no health_assessment, no validation_run and no satisfaction claim have been PRODUCED
outgoing: implementation wires itself into the field -> ReadingCollider

rejected: a log file or an export — read only by whoever already knows to look, which is never the person who needs it

attaching the stele PART_OF the orientation beacon: that is exactly the un-founded containment the inscription records, and repeating it to gain a tidy tree would make the stele an instance of its own cautionary tale
building a dormitory Space or a district to hold the bodies: an open design decision that belongs to the operator, not to the object that merely remembers why it is open
flattening the inscription into a single narrative paragraph: it reads better and it silently promotes every inference to a measurement
dropping the operator's `PART_OF = 0` and inscribing only the measured count: it destroys the record of the belief
dropping the operator's 1.0932 m because this builder did not re-measure it: absence of re-measurement is not grounds for deletion, it is grounds for the status `reported`
authoring a Built pose so the stele renders somewhere pleasant — a chosen-looking coordinate nobody chose
a periodic broadcast of the lore to everyone nearby: a construct that scrutes, and the loudest object in the city
why: A city that keeps no lore re-derives its accidents forever. The dormitory ball was diagnosed once, at cost, from a rendered frame; without a stele the next observer starts from the same frame with none of the diagnosis.
The lore must reach the person STANDING in the place, which is why the trigger is a body crossing a collider and not a query anyone has to think to run.

Storing claims rather than prose is what keeps a memory from decaying into a myth: each statement carries what kind of thing it is and who established it, so a later reader can tell the 1.0932 m (reported, solver-derived) from the 1.00 m (measured, a kernel constant) from 'it was never designed' (inferred).

Carrying the CONTEST rather than silently correcting it preserves the one fact a correction would erase — that the city held a false belief about its own structure — which is exactly the kind of thing a memorial is for.
Sealing, and making an unsealed inscription non-conductive, means a tampered stele goes silent rather than lying. A memorial that can be edited without notice is worse than none.
Declaring the stance and leaving it empty, rather than authoring a coordinate, keeps the stele from committing in its own body the confusion its first inscription is about.

content.composition_rule: healthy requires every all_required dimension measured and passing, every applicable dimension fresh within its TTL, and the observer rung at fixture_verified or above. Any dimension not_measured yields not_measured overall — never a lower-confidence `healthy`. Any dimension past TTL yields stale. A failed measurement yields measurement_failed, which is distinct from a measured failure.

current_sample.note: Zero of the fourteen dimensions have a sample: the stele has never been wired, has never been crossed, and carries no seal. This is `not_measured`, which is not zero and not a failure.

contest_completeness.measured_by: per contested claim, assert both as_received and as_measured are present in the delivered payload

cooldown_respected.measured_by: minimum interval between two reveals to the same body in the ledger, against the declared cooldown_ms

delivery_evidence.measured_by: a delivery record exists for the exact payload hash; an emitter fire alone is not counted

energy_conservation_error.measured_by: sum of deposited minus conducted minus consumed integer energy over the atom ledger

epistemic_status_preservation.composition: all_required — one upgraded status caps health at degraded
epistemic_status_preservation.measured_by: per claim, compare stored epistemic_status to delivered epistemic_status

evidence_freshness_seconds.composition: gate — a vector past any dimension's TTL derives `stale`, never that dimension's last value
evidence_freshness_seconds.measured_by: now minus the oldest sample's measured_at in this vector

measured_stream_only_rate.measured_by: fraction of conducted bonds whose energy_status is measured

not_measured_honesty_rate.measured_by: fraction of unmeasurable dimensions reported as not_measured rather than as 0 or as a pass

observer_trust_rung.composition: caps — below fixture_verified every proof it feeds is WEAK
observer_trust_rung.measured_by: the highest ladder rung this observer's own validation run earned

payload_fidelity.measured_by: byte-compare the delivered claim set against the stored claim set

physics_event_inertness.composition: all_required — a mutating physics event is a hard failure
physics_event_inertness.measured_by: committed store byte-identical across the physics wave containing the crossing

reader_correctness.measured_by: the delivered reader_body_key equals the body reported by the crossing event

reveal_uniqueness.composition: all_required — any value above 0 is a failure
reveal_uniqueness.measured_by: count reveals per crossing_event_id in the reading ledger

seal_valid.composition: all_required — an invalid seal is a hard failure, not a degradation
seal_valid.measured_by: recompute the hash over the stored inscription bytes and compare to the sealed hash

content.success_condition: For each fresh admitted approach by an identified citizen body, and only while the inscription set's seal is measured valid, exactly one `revealed_inscription` stimulus is delivered to that exact reader, carrying every inscribed claim VERBATIM together with its own epistemic status (measured / observed / inferred / reported / contested / unknown / not_measured), the revision and universe it was observed at, and who observed it. A claim whose status is `inferred` is never delivered as `measured`. A contested claim is delivered WITH its contest, never with only one side. A broken seal reveals nothing and yields `measurement_failed`. No reveal occurs without an approach that physically happened, and no approach yields two reveals inside the declared cooldown.

content.freshness: Past its fresh_until the state is `stale`, never its last value. A claim is never inherited from a prior revision of this construct.

It does NOT trust the implementation's own status fields, the renderer's 'revealed' flag, the emitter's fire, or the presence of a receipt.

content.trust_rung_justification: This observer has never run. It has not read anything back, so it has not earned `observed`; it has not been put in front of the fault-injection fixture in memory-stele-observer-v0, so it is nowhere near `fixture_verified`. Every proof it would feed is WEAK, and it says so before it is asked.

content.chain: reading collider -> physics crossing -> DepositBond (+measured energy) -> approach atom -> threshold (support >= N) -> reveal gate (5 measured supports) -> terminal emitter -> ONE revealed_inscription -> reveal_receipt + reading_ledger -> independent observer -> metric vector -> health -> satisfaction claim
content.epistemic_honesty: An inscribed memory is not a measured fact. This pattern therefore refuses to carry a claim without its status: the stele's unit of storage is not a sentence but a CLAIM + STATUS + SOURCE + REVISION. A stele that flattened those into prose would be a more beautiful object and a worse one — the prose would read as measurement and the reader would have no way to tell.
content.loop_part: the design rationale and reusable shape
content.pattern: A dormant civic object holding a SEALED, append-structured set of inscriptions, plus one bounded reactive circuit: a reading collider placed in the field; a DepositBond that puts measured energy on an approach atom when a citizen body crosses it; a threshold that fires once; a reveal gate whose supports are approach-admitted, reader-identified, seal-valid, inscription-non-empty and dedup-token-fresh; and a TERMINAL emitter whose fire surfaces exactly one stimulus. An independent observer then re-reads the delivered payload against the stored inscription, byte for byte, and against each claim's declared epistemic status.
content.why_a_stele_and_not_a_log: A log is read by whoever goes looking. A stele is read by whoever ARRIVES — the lore reaches the person standing in the place the lore is about, which is the only place it is useful. That is why the trigger is a body crossing a collider and not a query.

content.loop_part: the terms of the stele and the conflations it forbids

terms.ApproachAtom: The trigger atom a crossing deposits measured energy onto. Fires at support >= N.
terms.Claim: The stele's unit of storage: { statement, epistemic_status, source, measured_by, observed_at_revision, universe }. Never a bare sentence.
terms.Contest: A claim the stele carries TOGETHER WITH a measurement that disagrees with it. Both sides, both provenances, and which one was re-measured by whom. A stele resolves nothing by deletion.
terms.DedupToken: The causal key that makes one crossing yield at most one reveal. Distinct from cooldown: the token prevents a double-fire on ONE crossing, the cooldown prevents a body loitering on the collider boundary from re-firing forever.
terms.EpistemicStatus: measured | observed | inferred | reported | contested | unknown | not_measured. Attached per claim, never per inscription — one inscription routinely mixes several.
terms.Inscription: One dated, sealed memory: a title, a narrative rendering, and the ordered CLAIMS the narrative rests on. An inscription without claims is a story; an inscription with claims is a record.
terms.ReadingCollider: The physical condition placed in the field: the stele's reading radius. Crossing it is the only thing that wakes this construct.
terms.ReadingLedger: The durable record of who read what, when, and under which seal — so a reveal that a renderer animated but never delivered is distinguishable from one that landed.
terms.RevealGate: The atom whose fire authorizes one reveal. Requires five measured supports; missing any one of them, it does not fire and the stele stays silent.
terms.RevealedInscription: The typed stimulus delivered to the exact reader, carrying the inscription verbatim with every claim's status attached.
terms.Seal: A signature over the exact inscription bytes. Valid seal => the text revealed is the text inscribed. Adding or revising an inscription BREAKS the seal until re-sealed.
terms.Stele: The placed civic object that holds lore about a place. One stance, one sealed inscription set, one reactive reveal circuit. It stores; it does not interpret.

notes: The member set comes from a bounded heuristic (id-suffix match + construct-internal relation closure + satellite content references). A member the heuristic does not reach is `unknown`, never `known_absent`.

This document is a definition read from the graph. It carries no runtime evidence: nothing here can say `healthy`, `correct` or `objective satisfied`. Absence of a runtime moment is reported, not interpreted.
The store is a durable projection, not the truth. The revision above states which view this was taken from; a later revision may hold something else.
